problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{{z}^{2}}$ that passes through the point $P(1,0,-1).$
worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0,-1) & =\frac{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{{z}^{2}} & =1 \\ {z}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,0,-1)$ is the cone ${z}^{2}={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}.$
